timeline_events.summary: David Appel is indicted for allegedly giving bribes to Ariel Sharon and Ehud Olmert in exchange for lobbying the Greek government.
Deputy Prime Minister Ehud Olmert says the prime minister does not intend to act against Yasser Arafat next week, today, or tomorrow, while reiterating the position in principle on Arafat's immunity.
Ehud Olmert is set to become joint Deputy Prime Minister with Shimon Peres as part of a new coalition government deal between Ariel Sharon's Likud and the Labour party.
Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon suffers a significant stroke and his authorities are transferred to his deputy Ehud Olmert.
Ehud Olmert gains support from other potential challengers, including Shimon Peres, to become acting prime minister and likely successor to Ariel Sharon.
Likud ministers defy their leader Binyamin Netanyahu's resignation order, with three drafting resignation letters but not submitting them to acting prime minister Ehud Olmert.
Ehud Olmert is formally chosen to lead the Kadima party into nationwide elections due in March and confirmed as Kadima chairman.

On the eve of Israel's Knesset election, acting prime minister Ehud Olmert's Kadima party slipped in final opinion polls to a predicted 34 seats, raising the prospect that he may need to form a coalition with hardline parties opposed to his West Bank withdrawal plan.

Exit polls show acting prime minister Ehud Olmert's Kadima Party winning Israel's election by a smaller margin than expected, with projections indicating Kadima would win between 29 to 32 seats in the 120-member parliament.
Acting Israeli prime minister Ehud Olmert begins building a coalition after his Kadima party won the general election.
The Israeli cabinet formally ended Ariel Sharon's premiership, declaring him permanently incapacitated, and appointed Ehud Olmert as his replacement.
Israel's cabinet declared Ariel Sharon permanently incapacitated, formalizing Ehud Olmert's role as prime minister.
Ehud Olmert, Israel's prime minister designate, sent a letter extending Mordechai Vanunu's ban on leaving Israel for another year.

Interim prime minister Ehud Olmert's Kadima party signed its first coalition agreement with the Pensioners' party, bringing him closer to the parliamentary majority needed for his plan to draw Israel's final borders by 2010.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert named a coalition cabinet line-up designed to push through a major withdrawal from West Bank settlements, with the government to be sworn in later that week.
Ehud Olmert heads the coalition government that was presented to parliament, following Ariel Sharon's stroke in January.

Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas telephoned Israeli prime minister Ehud Olmert to congratulate him and offer to resume peace negotiations, though Olmert's office said no date had been set for a meeting.

Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert visits Washington to meet with the Bush administration, but appears to back away from his proposal for unilateral West Bank disengagement amid US reluctance to endorse it.
Ehud Olmert made his first visit to Washington as Israel's prime minister while his predecessor Ariel Sharon remained in a coma.
Ehud Olmert arrives in London for his first meeting with Tony Blair since becoming Prime Minister of Israel.

Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert wavered between accepting a UN ceasefire resolution and ordering a full invasion of Lebanon, amid plummeting public approval and criticism of his wartime leadership.
A newspaper poll showed for the first time that a majority of Israelis (63%) wanted Prime Minister Ehud Olmert to resign over perceived failures in his handling of the war with Hizbullah.
A newspaper poll shows that for the first time a majority of Israelis (63%) want Prime Minister Ehud Olmert to resign over his handling of the war with Hizbullah.

Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert was interrupted by reserve soldiers heckling him and demanding his resignation during a Jewish new year speech, amid protests over Israel's conduct of the war in Lebanon.
The Israeli supreme court gave Ehud Olmert's government five days to explain why it refused to appoint a high-level inquiry into decision-making during the summer's war in Lebanon.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert brings rightwing politician Avigdor Lieberman into his coalition government, making him deputy prime minister responsible for strategic threats.

Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert offered to release Palestinian prisoners in exchange for the return of captured soldier Gilad Shalit and held out the possibility of renewed Middle East peace talks.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert accidentally acknowledged that Israel has nuclear weapons during an interview with Germany's Sat.1 channel, prompting calls for his resignation.

Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert faced accusations of ineptitude and calls for his resignation after he appeared to acknowledge for the first time that Israel had nuclear weapons, though he later insisted Israel's policy of nuclear ambiguity had not changed.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert faced fallout from the Lebanon war after the head of the armed forces, Lieutenant-General Dan Halutz, resigned.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert called on President Moshe Katsav to resign after the attorney general said he would charge Katsav with rape and other sexual offences.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert gave a defiant speech to his Kadima party, admitting he is unpopular but stating he intends to remain in office despite calls for his resignation.
The Winograd commission's interim report held Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert responsible for "very serious failings" over the 2006 Lebanon war, but Olmert refused to resign.
Israeli cabinet minister Eitan Cabel resigns in protest over Ehud Olmert's handling of the Lebanon war, calling for Olmert to resign, while Olmert refuses to step down.

Israeli foreign minister Tzipi Livni calls on Prime Minister Ehud Olmert to resign over his handling of last year's war in Lebanon, following the Winograd report's finding of a "serious failure in judgment, responsibility and prudence."
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert refuses to resign despite Foreign Minister Tzipi Livni and others urging him to step down following the Winograd committee report on the Lebanon war.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert told the Winograd commission that he blamed the military for failings in the Lebanon war, according to released testimony.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert announced he will release 250 Fatah prisoners from Israeli prisons as a goodwill gesture aimed at boosting Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert toured the border with Lebanon and declared last year's war with Hizbullah a success, despite two Israeli soldiers remaining in Hizbullah's hands.
Ehud Olmert announced his resignation as Israeli prime minister, effective September 17th, the date of the next Kadima party leadership primary.

Israel's attorney general orders a criminal investigation into Prime Minister Ehud Olmert's purchase of his Jerusalem home over allegations he received a discount in return for political favors, which Olmert denies.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert pledged to remain in office and continue his duties despite being diagnosed with prostate cancer, for which he will undergo surgery.

Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert loses his rightwing coalition partner, Avigdor Lieberman's Yisrael Beiteinu party, in protest at new peace talks with the Palestinians, reducing his coalition to 67 seats in the 120-member parliament.

The Winograd commission's final report on the 2006 Lebanon war found serious failings in Israel's political and military leadership but stopped short of severe personal criticism of Prime Minister Ehud Olmert, leaving him politically secure in the short term.

Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert faces renewed pressure to resign amid a reported high-level bribery investigation involving American millionaire Morris Talansky, though his office denies reports that he planned to quit or temporarily step down.

Opponents of Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert called for his resignation over allegations that he took hundreds of thousands of dollars in bribes from an American financier, after magistrates lifted a gagging order on details of the police investigation.

Corruption scandals engulfed Ehud Olmert's premiership as Israel celebrated its 60th birthday, with allegations that he received hundreds of thousands of dollars from US financier Morris Moshe Talansky and defrauded charities.
Israeli newspaper Yediot Ahronot reports that police suspect Prime Minister Ehud Olmert may have acted illegally in helping companies bid for government contracts.
Israeli police began questioning Prime Minister Ehud Olmert for a second time in a corruption case, with no charges filed against him.
US businessman Morris Talansky testified in Jerusalem district court that he gave Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert at least $150,000 in cash over 15 years, in a corruption investigation.

Israeli Defence Minister Ehud Barak called on Prime Minister Ehud Olmert to suspend, vacation, resign or declare himself incapacitated after US businessman Morris Talansky testified that he gave Olmert $150,000 in cash over 15 years.
Israeli Defence Minister Ehud Barak called on Prime Minister Ehud Olmert to step aside amid corruption allegations that Olmert received $150,000 in cash from a US businessman.

Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert said he would step down in September amid multiple corruption inquiries, including allegations he took more than $150,000 in cash from US businessman Morris Talansky.
Israel's ruling Kadima party will meet next week to decide on an internal vote on the leadership of Prime Minister Ehud Olmert, amid corruption allegations.

Ehud Olmert faces five investigations since becoming prime minister in 2006, including a case in which investigators are trying to determine whether he broke campaign finance and bribery laws by accepting at least $150,000 in donations from US businessman Morris Talansky.

Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert appeared to have negotiated a last-minute deal with Labour party leader Ehud Barak to head off a parliamentary vote that might have unseated his government, reportedly promising that his Kadima party will hold an internal leadership primary by September 25.
Israel's ruling Kadima party is set to choose a leader in September to replace Ehud Olmert as prime minister.

Israeli police questioned Prime Minister Ehud Olmert for a third time as part of a widening corruption investigation, saying they suspect him of "serious fraud," though he has not been charged and denies wrongdoing.
Lawyers for Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert began cross-examining key witness Moshe Talansky in a corruption investigation that could end Olmert's political career.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert announced he would resign in September after his Kadima party chooses a new leader, amid corruption allegations.
Ehud Olmert is to step down in September after being engulfed in a series of corruption charges.
Ehud Olmert resigns as prime minister of Israel to concentrate on clearing his name of corruption charges.

Israeli Foreign Minister Tzipi Livni, the favourite to replace Ehud Olmert as prime minister in the ruling Kadima party's leadership elections next month, said it was unlikely a peace agreement with the Palestinians would be reached this year.
Israeli police recommend that Prime Minister Ehud Olmert be indicted for bribery, money laundering, fraud, and breach of trust following an 18-month investigation.
Tzipi Livni urged Ehud Olmert to stick to his pledge to resign as prime minister after she became leader of Israel's largest party, Kadima.
Ehud Olmert confirmed his resignation as Israel's prime minister but will remain in power until a new government is formed.
Ehud Olmert is described as the newly-resigned predecessor of Tzipi Livni, who was elected Kadima leader.
Israeli Foreign Minister Tzipi Livni abandoned efforts to form a governing coalition, putting Israel on course for early elections while Ehud Olmert continues as a lame-duck prime minister.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert promised to release 250 Palestinian prisoners during a meeting with Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas in Jerusalem.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert faced fresh calls to step down from within his party and cabinet after the attorney general said he was considering bringing criminal charges for corruption.
Outgoing Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert said Israel will not sign off on a Gaza ceasefire without the release of an Israeli soldier held in Hamas-controlled territory.
Ehud Olmert bids farewell.
Israeli prosecutors charged former prime minister Ehud Olmert with corruption in three separate cases, including fraud and breach of trust.
Former Israeli prime minister Ehud Olmert appeared in a Jerusalem court at the start of a high-profile corruption trial, insisting he will be acquitted.
Israeli police believe former prime minister Ehud Olmert is the prime suspect in the Holyland bribery case, though he has not been charged or questioned and has protested his innocence.
Israeli fraud investigators began questioning former prime minister Ehud Olmert over suspicions he took bribes as part of the Holyland property scandal in Jerusalem.

Former Israeli prime minister Ehud Olmert was cleared of two corruption charges but convicted of breach of trust for granting illegal favours to a friend and business partner while serving as minister of industry, trade and labour, and was sentenced to four months' community service.

Former Israeli prime minister Ehud Olmert is considering a political comeback to challenge Binyamin Netanyahu in a general election, despite his recent conviction for breach of trust and a forthcoming bribery trial.
Ehud Olmert was found guilty of bribery by an Israeli court.
Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert is sentenced to six years in jail on bribery charges by a Tel Aviv court.

Former Israeli prime minister Ehud Olmert pleads with judges at his sentencing hearing in Jerusalem district court not to jail him in the Talansky corruption case, with Tony Blair and former Mossad head Meir Dagan submitting character references in his support.
Ehud Olmert was forced to resign, after which Tzipi Livni became leader of the Kadima party.
Ehud Olmert became leader of the Kadima party and acting prime minister of Israel in January 2006 when Ariel Sharon fell into a coma after suffering a stroke.

facts.text: On 2004-04-26, Deputy Prime Minister Ehud Olmert said the prime minister did not intend to act against Yasser Arafat next week, today, or tomorrow, while reiterating the position in principle on Arafat's immunity.
On 2004-12-19, Ehud Olmert was set to become joint Deputy Prime Minister with Shimon Peres as part of a new coalition deal between Ariel Sharon's Likud and the Labour party.
On 2006-01-04, Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon suffered a significant stroke and his authorities were transferred to his deputy Ehud Olmert.
On 2006-01-16, Ehud Olmert was formally chosen to lead the Kadima party into nationwide elections due in March and confirmed as Kadima chairman.
On 2006-04-11, Israel's cabinet declared Ariel Sharon permanently incapacitated, formalizing Ehud Olmert's role as prime minister.
On 2007-04-30, the Winograd commission's interim report held Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert responsible for "very serious failings" over the 2006 Lebanon war, but Olmert refused to resign.
On 2008-05-28, Israeli Defence Minister Ehud Barak called on Prime Minister Ehud Olmert to step aside amid corruption allegations that Olmert received $150,000 in cash from a US businessman.
On 2008-07-29, Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert announced he would resign in September after his Kadima party chooses a new leader, amid corruption allegations.

events.summary: Ehud Olmert is to step down in September after being engulfed in a series of corruption charges.
Ehud Olmert announced he was resigning as prime minister in response to growing corruption investigations into his affairs.
Ehud Olmert arrives in London for his first meeting with Tony Blair since becoming Prime Minister of Israel.

Interim prime minister Ehud Olmert's Kadima party signed its first coalition agreement with the Pensioners' party, bringing him closer to the parliamentary majority needed for his plan to draw Israel's final borders by 2010.

Ehud Olmert faces five investigations since becoming prime minister in 2006, including a case in which investigators are trying to determine whether he broke campaign finance and bribery laws by accepting at least $150,000 in donations from US businessman Morris Talansky.
Ehud Olmert announced his resignation as Israeli prime minister, effective September 17th, the date of the next Kadima party leadership primary.
Ehud Olmert confirmed his resignation as Israel's prime minister but will remain in power until a new government is formed.

Former Israeli prime minister Ehud Olmert is considering a political comeback to challenge Binyamin Netanyahu in a general election, despite his recent conviction for breach of trust and a forthcoming bribery trial.
Israel's ruling Kadima party is set to choose a leader in September to replace Ehud Olmert as prime minister.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert announced he would resign in September after his Kadima party chooses a new leader, amid corruption allegations.
Israeli police began questioning Prime Minister Ehud Olmert for a second time in a corruption case, with no charges filed against him.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert brings rightwing politician Avigdor Lieberman into his coalition government, making him deputy prime minister responsible for strategic threats.

Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert made a defiant speech to his Kadima party's governing council, admitting he was "an unpopular prime minister" but stating he intends to remain in office despite growing calls for his resignation ahead of a crucial war report.
Israeli police believe former prime minister Ehud Olmert is the prime suspect in the Holyland bribery case, though he has not been charged or questioned and has protested his innocence.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert gave a defiant speech to his Kadima party, admitting he is unpopular but stating he intends to remain in office despite calls for his resignation.
Ehud Olmert became leader of the Kadima party and acting prime minister of Israel in January 2006 when Ariel Sharon fell into a coma after suffering a stroke.

Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert said he would step down in September amid multiple corruption inquiries, including allegations he took more than $150,000 in cash from US businessman Morris Talansky.

Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert appeared to have negotiated a last-minute deal with Labour party leader Ehud Barak to head off a parliamentary vote that might have unseated his government, reportedly promising that his Kadima party will hold an internal leadership primary by September 25.
Israeli prosecutors charged former prime minister Ehud Olmert with corruption in three separate cases, including fraud and breach of trust.

Israeli Defence Minister Ehud Barak called on Prime Minister Ehud Olmert to suspend, vacation, resign or declare himself incapacitated after US businessman Morris Talansky testified that he gave Olmert $150,000 in cash over 15 years.

Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert visits Washington to meet with the Bush administration, but appears to back away from his proposal for unilateral West Bank disengagement amid US reluctance to endorse it.
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert pledged to remain in office and continue his duties despite being diagnosed with prostate cancer, for which he will undergo surgery.
Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert is sentenced to six years in jail on bribery charges by a Tel Aviv court.

Former Israeli prime minister Ehud Olmert was cleared of two corruption charges but convicted of breach of trust for granting illegal favours to a friend and business partner while serving as minister of industry, trade and labour, and was sentenced to four months' community service.
Former Israeli prime minister Ehud Olmert appeared in a Jerusalem court at the start of a high-profile corruption trial, insisting he will be acquitted.

Former Israeli prime minister Ehud Olmert pleads with judges at his sentencing hearing in Jerusalem district court not to jail him in the Talansky corruption case, with Tony Blair and former Mossad head Meir Dagan submitting character references in his support.
Lawyers for Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert began cross-examining key witness Moshe Talansky in a corruption investigation that could end Olmert's political career.
Israeli police recommend that Prime Minister Ehud Olmert be indicted for bribery, money laundering, fraud, and breach of trust following an 18-month investigation.
Israeli fraud investigators began questioning former prime minister Ehud Olmert over suspicions he took bribes as part of the Holyland property scandal in Jerusalem.
US businessman Morris Talansky testified in Jerusalem district court that he gave Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert at least $150,000 in cash over 15 years, in a corruption investigation.
